open_questions.question: Which records prove the subject's identity across events?
open_questions.current_conclusion: A specific daughter-in-law alternative can now be tested. Paterson’s 1866 county history, printed pp. 513–514 (PDF 249–250), says the elder Robert’s eldest son and heir, born 22 May 1811, married Mary-Wilhelmina, daughter of John Campbell of Stonefield, on 11 July 1839; their children include Wilhelmina-Colquhoun. The checked existing bride is Campbell-38211 and groom Robertson-Glasgow-11. A married Mary beside the infant of this same family could be that daughter-in-law rather than another daughter of the household head. This is a new comparison, not an established identification. The age problem remains real: FreeCEN gives Mary 19 in 1841, while Campbell-38211’s public profile gives 1816 and copies an 1851 age 34. The latter original is also unread. The infant’s full name and birth particulars are not established by FreeCEN. Paterson is a compiled family history, not an original marriage entry, and its adjacent Montgreenan descent narrative has known conflicts with the separately held court evidence. Do not transfer the book’s explicit John Campbell parentage to Glasgow-3021 before identifying the two Marys. Retain the selected Robert Robertson father at 45%, Jane’s father at 78%, all mother/vital fields and separate profiles; no father replacement, merge or confidence improvement is recorded. Checked candidate: https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Campbell-38211
